vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse-errors/negative-minimum-cardinality-is-invalid
vectors.comment: E.10: negative cardinality is rejected the same way as OSD text's `[-1]` (osd-grammar/cardinality/negative-minimum-is-invalid-not-a-syntax-error).

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse-errors/inverted-cardinality-range-is-invalid
vectors.comment: E.10: min > max is rejected the same way as OSD text's `[1,0]` (osd-grammar/cardinality/inverted-range-is-invalid).

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse-errors/zero-zero-cardinality-is-invalid
vectors.comment: E.5: `{ min: 0, max: 0 }` has no OSD spelling -- a field that can never appear is indistinguishable from an undeclared one. Inherited from the 2026-08-29 audit's `[0,0]` ban (osd-grammar/cardinality/zero-max-is-invalid-redundant-with-absence), not re-decided by this extension.

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse-errors/non-integer-cardinality-min-is-invalid
vectors.comment: Sec8.3.3: `min`/`max` not integer-kind reuses the existing `schema.non-integer-cardinality` code (previously only reachable via OSD text's own non-integer literal forms) -- OSD's grammar's `int` token guarantees the type there for a different reason (a bound is always a whole number when written), so this is the first input shape where a non-integer *value* in this position is possible at all.

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse-errors/non-string-field-label-is-invalid
vectors.comment: E.10: `field.label` must be string-kind. Also has no OSD-text analog -- OSD's grammar only ever produces a quoted-string label. `schema.invalid-type` is a general Schema-construction code defined in chapter 8, not owned by this extension.

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse-errors/empty-field-label-is-invalid
vectors.comment: E.10: same rejection as OSD text's empty-string label (osd-grammar/labels/empty-label-is-rejected), inherited unchanged.

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse-errors/bracket-in-field-label-is-invalid
vectors.comment: E.7: `[`/`]` in a field label is rejected the same way as OSD text (osd-grammar/labels/bracket-in-label-is-rejected) -- collides with validate's diagnostic-path convention regardless of surface syntax.

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse-errors/duplicate-record-name-is-invalid
vectors.comment: E.10: two `record` edges naming the same record is rejected the same way as OSD text's duplicate record definition (osd-grammar/reserved-names/duplicate-record-definition-is-an-error).

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse-errors/duplicate-field-label-is-invalid
vectors.comment: E.10: two `field` edges with the same label within one `record` is rejected the same way as OSD text (osd-grammar/records/duplicate-field-label-in-one-record-is-an-error).

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse-errors/reserved-record-name-is-invalid

input.text:
record: { name: "string", field: { label: "a", type: { kind: "any" } } }
root: "string"

vectors.comment: E.10: a record named after a scalar keyword is rejected the same way as OSD text (osd-grammar/reserved-names/record-named-after-a-scalar-keyword-is-rejected).

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse-errors/zero-root-edges-is-invalid

input.text: record: { name: "R", field: { label: "a", type: { kind: "any" } } }

vectors.comment: E.8: top-level `root` is [1,1], required. Zero `root` edges is rejected the same way as OSD text with no `root` declaration (osd-grammar/root/missing-root-is-an-error).

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse-errors/duplicate-root-edges-is-invalid
vectors.comment: E.8: top-level `root` is [1,1], at most one. Two `root` edges is rejected the same way as OSD text with two `root` declarations (osd-grammar/root/duplicate-root-is-an-error).

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse-errors/unresolved-reference-is-invalid
vectors.comment: E.6: a `ref` type's `name` must exact-match a declared `record.name`. `Ghost` is not a scalar keyword, not `any`, and not a defined record -- the same dangling-reference failure as OSD text (schema-wellformedness/refs/dangling-reference-is-an-error).

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse-errors/unknown-key-is-invalid
vectors.comment: 8.3.3: an unrecognized key anywhere in the Document shape is rejected -- `bogus` is not one of `label`/`type`/`cardinality` on a `field` node. `schema.unknown-key` is defined in chapter 8 as a general Schema-construction rule, with no OSD-text analog since its grammar has no way to write a stray key at all.

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse-errors/missing-required-key-is-invalid
vectors.comment: 8.3.3: `field.type` is [1,1] (E.8) but absent here entirely. `schema.missing-key` is a general Schema-construction rule with no OSD-text analog -- OSD's grammar has no production for a field with no type, so this case cannot be written in OSD text at all.

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/parse-errors/invalid-scalar-name-is-invalid
vectors.comment: 8.3.3: `schema.unknown-type` already covers 'resolves to neither a scalar nor a defined record' generally -- `bogus` is not one of the seven scalar keywords, so a `kind: "scalar"` naming it fails the same way a dangling `ref` does. Not a new code; this vector exercises the existing code's scalar-name half, which OSD text can never reach on its own (its grammar only ever produces one of the seven real keywords in this position).
